name: statement_import
description: Read a bank CSV export into the local ledger. Columns are detected from the headers (date, description, one signed amount or a debit and a credit column, currency, balance), amounts are read in the file's own locale, and every line already stored is skipped rather than doubled. Returns what was detected, what was stored, and what was skipped and why.

arguments.name: path
arguments.desc: Path to the .csv file exported from the bank. ~ is expanded

arguments.name: account
arguments.desc: Name for this account, e.g. "business EUR". Default: the file name without its extension. Later imports of the same account are deduplicated against it

arguments.name: bank
arguments.desc: Bank profile. Default "auto": the headers decide. "generic" skips profile detection and uses the header heuristics alone

arguments.name: overwrite
arguments.desc: Delete every transaction already stored for this account before importing, instead of merging. Use it when the bank reissued a corrected export

arguments.name: currency
arguments.desc: Currency for rows where the file names none. Without it EUR is assumed and the response says so

name: transactions_list
description: List stored transactions in a date range, optionally for one account or category, or only the ones no rule has categorised yet. Totals are reported per currency and never added across currencies.

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Default: the start of the current month

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Default: today

arguments.name: account
arguments.desc: Limit to one account, as named at import

arguments.name: category
arguments.desc: Only transactions in this category

arguments.name: uncategorized
arguments.desc: Only transactions with no category yet

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: Rows returned, default 200. Totals always cover the whole range

name: transactions_search
description: Find transactions whose description, counterparty, category or account contains the query. Case-insensitive substring search, never a regex, so a query with brackets in it cannot hang the server.

arguments.name: query
arguments.desc: Text to look for, e.g. "spotify" or "acme"

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: limit
arguments.desc: Rows returned, default 100

name: category_rules
description: Set the rules that categorise transactions, or call with no arguments to list them. Each rule is matched against the counterparty and the description: a plain match is a case-insensitive substring, and regex: true compiles it only when the pattern cannot backtrack exponentially. Setting rules re-applies them to every stored transaction that has no category yet.

arguments.name: rules
arguments.desc: The complete rule list; it replaces the stored one. Omit to list the current rules

arguments.name: reapply_all
arguments.desc: Also overwrite categories set by an earlier rule or by hand. Default false: only uncategorised transactions are touched

name: transaction_categorize
description: Set the category on one or more transactions by id. Nothing is changed unless every id exists, so a typo cannot half-apply.

arguments.name: ids
arguments.desc: Transaction ids, as returned by transactions_list or transactions_search

arguments.name: category
arguments.desc: Category to set. Pass an empty string to clear it

name: statement_summary
description: Money in, money out and the net for a date range, grouped by category, month, account or counterparty. Every total is reported per currency; amounts in different currencies are never added together and never converted.

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive. Default: the start of the current month

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive. Default: today

arguments.name: group_by
arguments.desc: Default category

arguments.name: account
arguments.desc: Limit the summary to one account

arguments.name: top
arguments.desc: Groups returned per currency, largest net first. Default 25

name: reconcile_expenses
description: Match bank debits against the expenses recorded by mcp-expense-tracker: same currency, same amount, and a date within a few days. Reports what matched, which bank lines have no expense behind them and which expenses never reached the bank. The expense ledger is only ever read, never written.

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: account
arguments.desc: Limit to one bank account

arguments.name: window_days
arguments.desc: Allowed gap between the expense date and the bank date, default 3. A card payment usually settles a day or two after the receipt

name: recurring_detect
description: Find the charges that come back: the same counterparty, an amount that barely moves and a steady cadence. Reports the cadence, the typical amount, when it was last taken, when it is next due and what it costs per year, per currency.

arguments.name: months
arguments.desc: How far back to look, default 3. Two occurrences are enough to see a cadence, three make it certain

arguments.name: account
arguments.desc: Limit to one account

arguments.name: min_occurrences
arguments.desc: Occurrences required before a charge counts as recurring, default 2

name: statement_export
description: Write the transactions of a date range to a .csv or .json file and return the path. The file is written atomically, so a failed export never leaves a half-written file behind.

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: ISO date, inclusive

arguments.name: format
arguments.desc: csv for a spreadsheet, json for a program

arguments.name: path
arguments.desc: Where to write the file. ~ is expanded; the parent directory must exist

arguments.name: account
arguments.desc: Limit to one account

arguments.name: category
arguments.desc: Limit to one category

name: accounts_list
description: List the imported accounts with their bank, currency, transaction count and date range.

name: license_status
description: Show whether this server runs in free or Pro mode and where to upgrade.

name: license_activate
description: Activate a Pro license key (format MCPL1.xxx.yyy). Verified offline and saved locally.

arguments.name: key
arguments.desc: License key from the checkout confirmation page
